 WTA Guangzhou Day 1 Predictions Including Paula Badosa vs Carol Young Suh Lee 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 It is the opening day of the WTA 250 event in Guangzhou , as another tournament on the Asian swing is set to commence. We have a packed slate of first-round matches on the day, with an exciting fixture list in store for all those in attendance and viewing around the world. As always, we here at LWOT will be predicting each match for you, but who do you think will make the second round?
 WTA Guangzhou Day 1 Predictions
 Han Shi vs Alevtina Ibragimova
 Head-to-head: Shi 0-1 Ibragimova
 Given a wildcard to play in front of her home fans in Guangzhou this week, Han Shi will face Alevtina Ibragimova in the opening round. Ibragimova played some decent tennis during the qualifying round, using her counterpunching skills effectively. This match will be determined from the back of the court, and from there Ibragimova has the edge. The home crowd energy should lift Shi’s level, but expect the Russian to win.
 Prediction: Ibragimova in 3 
 Harriet Dart vs Tatiana Prozorova
 Head-to-head: First meeting
 Both players have reached the main draw after coming through the qualifying round, so they should now be well versed with the surface and playing conditions. Dart will rely on her all-court finesse, while Prozorova will look to be the more consistent and solid player from the back of the court. I expect this match to be close, but Prozorova’s superior ball quality should eventually prove to be the difference.
 Prediction: Prozorova in 3 
 Paula Badosa vs Carol Young Suh Lee
 Head-to-head: First meeting
 Jan 23, 2025; Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; Paula Badosa of Spain plays a backhand during her match against Aryna Sabalenka in the semifinals of the women’s singles at the 2025 Australian Open at Melbourne Park. Mandatory Credit: Mike Frey-Imagn Images 
 Reaching the main draw after playing some solid aggressive tennis in the qualifying round, Carol Young Suh Lee faces former Top 10 player Paula Badosa in her opening match. Badosa is now far removed from her best tennis due to recurring injuries, but she can still play some decent counterpunching tennis on her day. Lee’s serve will be crucial here, as from the baseline the Spaniard should have the advantage. That advantage ultimately should see Badosa reach the next round here.
 Prediction: Badosa in 3
